messages:
alex_cs: FYI customer ACME sent a service key created via SSO and they're getting 403 on generation calls. embeddings and rerank seem to work.
julia_cse: can you paste the raw error they see? any request ids?
alex_cs: here's the curl they ran and the response. customer is on eu-west region.
alex_cs: ```bash
curl -X POST \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \ 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_sso_...\" \ 
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \ 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-1","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":10}'
```
alex_cs: response:
alex_cs: ```json
{"error":{"type":"insufficient_scope","message":"missing scope: inference.generate","hint":"key only has: embeddings.read"}}
```
maria_support: interesting that embeddings.read works but inference.generate missing. did they request a mixed scope key from SSO flow?
alex_cs: customer claims they clicked the standard "service-key" button in our SSO app. they expected both embeddings+generation.
julia_cse: @kai_provisioning can you check the SSO provisioning logs for that org (acme-corp) around when the key was created? maybe group mappings changed.
kai_provisioning: on it. provisioning bot shows a sync at 1956007200 with a warning about unmapped groups. pinging provisioner-bot for details.
provisioner-bot: [provisioner] create_service_key: org_id=acme-corp, actor=alice.admin, flow=SSO, requested_scopes=[embeddings.read,inference.generate,rerank.read]
provisioner-bot: [provisioner] result: created_key_id=srv_abc123, granted_scopes=[embeddings.read,rerank.read]
ben_oncall: aha — the provisioner dropped inference.generate. possible mapping rule excluded the "ml-infer" group.
alex_cs: any idea why we would drop one of the requested scopes? that's a bug in mapping logic or an admin policy.
kai_provisioning: looking at the mapping rules: we only auto-grant inference.generate if user is in group 'model-inference' or has role 'ml-service'. seems the admin removed that group mapping last week.
maria_support: customer says their identity admin removed old group names during org clean-up. they didn't realize policy change would affect scope grants.
julia_cse: next steps: 1) temporary workaround, create a manual service key with full scopes and give to customer; 2) remediate provisioning rule or make the error clearer in UI; 3) notify customer admin.
alex_cs: customer prefers not to have a manual key. they want SSO flow fixed.
kai_provisioning: I'll re-run the provisioning sync for that org after mapping update. but we should also return an explicit error in create_service_key flow when requested scopes are stripped, so callers see a 200 with smaller scopes currently which is confusing.en_oncall: agreed. escape hatch for now: api to re-request missing scopes: POST /internal/provisioner/keys/sync?org=acme-corp
maria_support: repro steps I used locally to simulate:
maria_support: ```bash
# simulate user with SSO groups missing 'model-inference'
export RB_USER_GROUPS=\"employees,dev\"
./local-provisioner create-service-key --org acme-corp --requested-scopes embeddings.read,inference.generate,rerank.read
# response shows granted scopes
{
  "key_id": "srv_test",
  "granted_scopes": ["embeddings.read","rerank.read"]
}
```
maria_support: error from client side then mirrors the live error above: 403 insufficient_scope.
julia_cse: thanks — can you paste the admin UX flow screenshot where we do the mapping? we need to make the dropped scopes visible.
alex_cs: attached screenshot in thread (customer redacted). they want us to add an explicit note during SSO key creation: "Some requested scopes may be rejected by organization policy. Confirm granted scopes." :thinking:
kai_provisioning: I'll add a quick fix to the provisioning service to return 207 (multistatus) with a list of requested vs granted scopes so callers can surface it. I'll also run a one-off sync for ACME and confirm.
provisioner-bot: [action] queued: sync_scopes org=acme-corp, initiated_by=kai_provisioning
maria_support: escalation asked for an ETA to present to customer — can we get the sync done and confirm within 2 hours?
ben_oncall: I can run the sync now and validate keys. will report back.
alex_cs: please also redact the secret in that key and rotate if we end up re-granting via manual path.
ben_oncall: sync complete. provisioner log: grant updated for srv_abc123: added inference.generate. tested a quick call and completions now succeed.
ben_oncall: test curl returned 200 and token used: "granted_scopes":["embeddings.read","inference.generate","rerank.read"]
alex_cs: relaying to customer. they asked that we add a permanent fix so future SSO-created keys surface scope differences and throw a clear error when requested scopes are dropped.
julia_cse: filing a product ticket for scope-visibility in SSO create flow, assign to infra/provisioner.
kai_provisioning: created ticket INFRA-7123, linking logs and repro. I'll also add audit events when scopes are filtered.
maria_support: closing loop with customer: suggested they remap their SSO groups to include 'model-inference' or request provisioning flag. customer is happy with patch and wants follow-up once ticket done. :thumbsup:
alex_cs: thanks team. notes: rotate key if used in the wild, add postmortem entry to incidents channel about confusing 200-with-missing-scopes behavior.
julia_cse: adding to <#incidents> later. thanks everyone.
